explore-forward.title: Which way does it conduct?
explore-forward.prompt: Find a voltage where the diode conducts.
hints: Negative voltages reverse bias the diode.
Go above about 0.7 V, anode positive.
explore-forward.success: Forward biased past about 0.6 V, it conducts. Any negative voltage, reverse biased, gives no current: it conducts one way only.

explore-rectifier.title: AC in, what comes out?
explore-rectifier.prompt: AC on the anode (dashed). What do you see at the cathode (solid)?
explore-rectifier.success: Only the positive halves get through: pulsating DC. That's rectification.

explore-zener.title: The Zener
explore-zener.prompt: Reverse bias this Zener (negative volts) until it starts to conduct backwards and hold its voltage.
explore-zener.success: Past −5.1 V it conducts in reverse and the voltage across it stays at 5.1 V however hard you push. That's regulation.
